headline: ADYTON DRILLS 167M AT 1.14 G/T AUEQ FROM SURFACE AT FENI ISLAND — KABANG AU-CU SYSTEM EXTENDS PAST 2KM WITH 7,500M ASSAYS STILL PENDING
snippet: Adyton Resources Corp (TSXV: ADY) reported September 15 assay results from 12 drill holes at its Kabang Au-Cu system at the 1.46moz Feni Island Gold-Copper Project in Papua New Guinea — highlight hole FDD026 returned 167 metres at 1.14 g/t AuEq from surface, confirming a structurally controlled system now traced over more than 2km of strike and open both northeast and southwest. With over 18,000 metres drilled in 2026 and approximately 7,500 metres of assays still pending, the company is targeting both an upgrade to the Indicated category and further definition of high-grade northeast and southwest extensions.

headline: RESOLUTION MINERALS HITS 14.8 G/T GOLD AT HORSE HEAVEN, IDAHO — GOLDEN GATE SOUTH ZONE NOW 600 METRES WIDE WITH HIGH-GRADE FEEDER VEINS CONFIRMED
snippet: Resolution Minerals Ltd (ASX: RML) announced September 15 the highest gold grades recorded to date at its Horse Heaven Antimony-Tungsten-Gold-Silver Project in Idaho — best hole HH-GG26-004C returned 7.2 metres at 2.35 g/t gold including 1 metre at 14.8 g/t gold and 12 g/t silver, while adjacent HH-GG26-005C intersected 10.2 metres at 1.83 g/t gold. The results extend the Golden Gate South mineralized zone to approximately 600 metres wide, with the presence of high-grade feeder intervals suggesting an intact hydrothermal system with potential for higher-grade cores at depth.

headline: GETTY COPPER DRILLS 46M AT 1.47% COPPER WITHIN 150M AT 0.71% — TWO RIGS MOBILIZING TO GETTY SOUTH IN BC'S HIGHLAND VALLEY DISTRICT
snippet: Getty Copper Inc (TSXV: GTC) reported September 14 spring 2026 drill assay results from Getty South in the Highland Valley District of British Columbia — step-out holes returned 150 metres at 0.71% copper including 46 metres at 1.47% copper and a 7.5-metre interval grading 3.72% copper, intersecting high-grade breccia mineralization described as unique within the district. The company is accelerating follow-up drilling with two rigs mobilizing to Getty South in late September to define the size and continuity of the high-grade zone and test adjacent exploration targets.

headline: COPPER'S $14,533 RECORD GIVES BACK 5% IN ONE SESSION — WHITE HOUSE TARIFF STALL ENDS MINERS' BEST RUN SINCE JUNE
snippet: Copper fell nearly 5% on September 12 after reports that the White House had stalled its plan to impose tariffs on imported refined copper — officials reportedly feared the levies could push domestic prices even higher — erasing roughly $700 per tonne from its LME record of US$14,533 and handing copper its first weekly loss since June. The three-month contract settled near US$14,233 before steadying toward US$14,000 on September 15 as underlying supply constraints from Codelco and Freeport-McMoRan production declines and an ongoing sulfuric acid shortage reasserted themselves.

headline: CHINA LITHIUM DATA REVISION DOUBLES STOCKPILES OVERNIGHT — FUTURES CRASH 14% IN THREE SESSIONS, GANFENG THREATENS TO ABANDON BENCHMARKS
snippet: Chinese pricing agency SMM altered its lithium carbonate inventory sampling methodology on September 4, causing reported stockpiles to jump to 175,000 tonnes from 78,800 — a near-doubling with zero change in physical stocks — and sending the most-active January lithium carbonate futures contract on the Guangzhou Futures Exchange down more than 14% across three sessions to roughly 134,800 yuan (~US$20,100) per tonne. Ganfeng Lithium publicly threatened to abandon third-party price benchmarks in response, while SQM shed 8.6% for the week through September 12, amplifying the confusion over China's actual lithium supply position.

headline: BANNERMAN ETANGO URANIUM FULLY FUNDED — A$124M PLACED, CNNC JV CONDITIONS MET, NAMIBIAN PROJECT TARGETING Q4 FINAL INVESTMENT DECISION
snippet: Bannerman Energy (ASX: BMN) has completed a fully underwritten A$124 million (US$89 million) equity placement and confirmed all conditions precedent to CNNC Overseas Limited's strategic joint venture investment in its Etango uranium project in Namibia have been satisfied — fully funding its 55% share of project costs through construction and ramp-up. With financing secured, Bannerman is targeting a final investment decision and commencement of full-scale construction in Q4 2026; the new feasibility study projects a nine-year mine life producing 13.8 million pounds of U3O8.

headline: SILVER'S SIXTH STRAIGHT ANNUAL DEFICIT AT 46.3M OZ UNCHANGED — CRUX INVESTOR: FED HAWKS ARE TESTING THE FLOOR, NOT BREAKING THE THESIS
snippet: Crux Investor's pre-FOMC analysis argues that the Federal Reserve's hawkish pivot — with Chair Warsh and Governor Cook both signalling September hike support — is testing silver's $63 support level but is not dismantling the structural case: the Silver Institute's World Silver Survey 2026 projects a sixth consecutive annual deficit of 46.3 million ounces and a cumulative drawdown of 762.1 million ounces of above-ground stocks since 2021. The piece frames the setup as asymmetric: real-yield pressure sets this week's price while the supply math reasserts itself once the rate picture stabilizes.

headline: CHINA ESCALATES JAPAN RARE EARTH REVIEWS AS NOVEMBER 10 EXPORT CONTROL DEADLINE LOOMS — $6.5T IN DOWNSTREAM PRODUCTION AT RISK
snippet: China has imposed stricter licensing review measures on rare earth exports to Japan amid escalating bilateral tensions, adding urgency as the 12-month suspension of China's expanded rare earth export controls is set to expire on November 10, 2026. China processes up to 90% of global rare earth supply; the IEA estimates that full reimplementation of controls could place US$6.5 trillion of downstream production outside China at risk and displace up to 13,000 tonnes of annual demand to non-Chinese producers — a structural tailwind for developers including MP Materials (already partnered with Saudi Arabia's Ma'aden), Energy Fuels, and USA Rare Earth.

headline: GOLDMAN $4,900, JPMORGAN $4,500: MAJOR BANKS HOLD GOLD TARGETS UNCHANGED AS RETAIL INVESTORS SELL INTO $4,263 PRE-FOMC DIP
snippet: Major banks have not adjusted their gold price targets despite the metal's fall to a five-week low of $4,263 ahead of Wednesday's Fed decision — Goldman Sachs holds a 2026 year-end target of $4,900, JPMorgan's Q4 target is $4,500, Bank of America's 2026 average is $4,360, and HSBC's is $4,560 — with analysts noting the 25-basis-point hike was already priced at 92% certainty. CBS News summarizes the consensus: what markets need to watch is not the hike itself but the forward guidance, as any hawkish November signal could extend short-term pressure on gold and junior mining equities.

headline: GOLD AND SILVER AT CRITICAL SUPPORT AHEAD OF FOMC — FXEMPIRE MAPS THE LEVELS THAT BREAK DOWN IF WEDNESDAY'S STATEMENT TURNS HAWKISH
snippet: FX Empire's pre-FOMC technical analysis identifies the key levels for gold and silver heading into the Federal Reserve's September 16 decision — gold's five-week low at $4,263 is the first critical test with $4,200 as the next significant support, while silver's $63 floor sits at a level where the structural deficit case begins to attract longer-term buyers. The analysis frames three scenarios for each metal depending on whether the FOMC language is neutral, hawkish, or signals a November pause, and notes that gold has bottomed within six weeks of the first post-pause rate hike in every tightening cycle since 2015.
